title: refactor: parse all usage headers as numbers
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Follow-up to #15129.

- `parseUsageHeaders()` parses every `x-usage-*` header with `Number()` — the exact inverse of the `String(number)` that `buildUsageHeaders` writes. Removes the `FLOAT_USAGE_TYPES` allowlist whose `parseInt` fallback caused #15129, so a future fractional unit can't silently truncate again.
- No behavior change for integer token counts; fractional units (seconds, image megapixels) parse exactly, same as after #15129.

The Tinybird column widening that was in this PR is split out into draft #15134 (speculative: needs a staging probe on `UInt32` truncation-vs-rejection and carries heavy table rebuilds; the telemetry shape for fractional units is an open architecture question).

gist.headline: Fractions Get Their Due
gist.blurb: The usage meter now counts the small bits too. Seconds and image megapixels can pass through the hive without being rounded into administrative pollen dust.
gist.summary: `parseUsageHeaders()` now parses every `x-usage-*` header with `Number()`, exactly reversing `buildUsageHeaders()`'s `String(number)` serialization and preventing fractional usage units such as seconds or image megapixels from being truncated.
gist.impact: Integer token counts behave exactly as before, while current and future fractional usage values retain their full precision through usage-event parsing.
